name: GL_INTERFACE
description: GL_INTERFACE contains journal entry batches through Journal Import. You insert rows in this table and then use the Import Journals window to create journal batches. You must supply values for all NOT NULL columns. For a complete description of how to load this table, see the Oracle General Ledger User Guide.

columns.name: STATUS
columns.description: Journal Import status.  Use: NEW.

columns.name: JOURNAL_ATTACHMENTS
columns.description: Add attachments using URLs to General Ledger journal batches when creating single journals in the ADFdi Create Journal spreadsheet

columns.name: GL_INTERFACE_ID
columns.description: Interface Identifier.  Oracle internal use only. Populated by the journal import program.

columns.name: CREATION_DATE
columns.description: Who column: date and time of the creation of the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_DATE
columns.description: Who column: date and time of the last update of the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_LOGIN
columns.description: Who column: session login associated to the user who last updated the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATED_BY
columns.description: Who column: user who last updated the row.

columns.name: OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER
columns.description: Used to implement optimistic locking. Incremented every time the row is updated.  Compared at the start and end of a transaction to detect whether another session has updated the row since it was queried.

columns.name: LEDGER_ID
columns.description: Ledger identifier.  Use the Manage Primary Ledgers task to find valid values.

columns.name: JE_SOURCE_NAME
columns.description: Oracle internal use only.  Use column USER_JE_SOURCE_NAME to populate journal source.

columns.name: JE_CATEGORY_NAME
columns.description: Oracle internal use only.  Use column USER_JE_CATEGORY_NAME to populate journal category.

columns.name: ACCOUNTING_DATE
columns.description: Effective date of the journal entry.  Used to assign the accounting period.

columns.name: CURRENCY_CODE
columns.description: Entered currency of the transaction.  Use the Manage Currencies task to find valid values.  Use the three character ISO currency code.  Example: US Dollars is USD.

columns.name: DATE_CREATED
columns.description: Who column: date the row was created.

columns.name: CREATED_BY
columns.description: Who column: user who created the row.

columns.name: ACTUAL_FLAG
columns.description: Balance type of the journal.  Use: A.  Meaning:  Actual.

columns.name: REQUEST_ID
columns.description: Enterprise Service Scheduler: request ID of the job that created or last updated the row.

columns.name: ENCUMBRANCE_TYPE_ID
columns.description: Oracle internal use only.

columns.name: BUDGET_VERSION_ID
columns.description: Oracle internal use only.

columns.name: CURRENCY_CONVERSION_DATE
columns.description: Date of exchange rate.  Date format:  YYYY/MM/DD.  Required if CURRENCY_CONVERSION_TYPE is  not User.

columns.name: CURRENCY_CONVERSION_TYPE
columns.description: Currency conversion type. Use Manage Currency Conversion Types task to identify valid values. For Fusion ERP in the Cloud, use USER_CURRENCY_CONVERSION_TYPE instead.

columns.name: CURRENCY_CONVERSION_RATE
columns.description: Foreign currency exchange rate.  Mandatory if CURRENCY_CONVERSION_TYPE is User.
